rewrites.comment: The app uses client-side routing, so every path has to be served index.html. Without this, a shared link like /sorting?algo=quick&seed=2024 would 404 — the server has no such file.

headers.comment: Security headers for every response. The CSP allows only this origin, plus wandbox.org for the compiled IDE languages. It needs 'unsafe-eval' because the IDE runs reader code with new Function inside blob: workers, and a blob: worker inherits the page's policy. It needs style 'unsafe-inline' because Monaco injects style elements and the bars are sized with inline styles. vite.config.ts serves the same headers from `vite preview`, so the end-to-end suite runs under this exact policy.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self' blob:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data:; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https://wandbox.org; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.comment: Every route is rewritten to index.html, so the no-cache rule has to cover all of them, not just /index.html. With cleanUrls on, a request for /index.html is a 301 to /, which means a rule matching only /index.html never applies to a real request and every page fell through to Firebase's default max-age=3600. A returning visitor could then hold a stale entry point pointing at asset hashes the deploy had already removed.
Vite fingerprints asset filenames, so they can be cached forever. Defined after the catch-all because the last matching rule wins.
